ranges.quote: A two hundred character link becomes six characters. Simple idea, surprisingly neat system.
ranges.reason: Take 2 of 2. Take 1 (16.58) aborts at 21.27 on 'Surprising idea, s...' and uses the wrong adjective.

ranges.quote: So you might think it hashes the URL, but you want the shortest possible code and no collisions. Random hashing gives you neither cleanly.
ranges.reason: Single clean take across both sentences.

ranges.quote: Instead, every new link gets a unique number from a counter, one, two, three, and so on. Then we encode that number in Base62.
ranges.reason: Single clean take. The counter recital lands at 54.08-54.94, which is where the overlay's counter ticks.

ranges.quote: Base62 uses zero through nine, lowercase a through z, and capital A through Z, sixty-two symbols.
ranges.reason: Take 4 of 4. Takes 1-3 (59.12, 78.68, 81.76) all abort mid-alphabet. Take 4 also beats the only other complete read (68.52) on safety: 68.52 runs straight into an aborted 'So big numbers become...' leaving just 240ms to cut in, while this take has 6.0s of dead air after it. Its 660ms pause before 'sixty-two' is a gift for the overlay -- the alphabet assembles, then the count lands.

ranges.quote: So big numbers become tiny strings. Just three characters cover almost a quarter million links. Six cover over fifty billion.
ranges.reason: Clean completion of the sentence take 1 aborted on, spliced to the Base62 take.

ranges.quote: Visiting the short link looks up the number and redirects you to the original.
ranges.reason: Contiguous with SCALE in the source and the better of the two reads -- the 118.98 retake is slower and boxes 'original.' out to 124.22 against an acoustic end of 123.51. Kept as its own range so the lookup/redirect gets its own overlay.

ranges.quote: Every short link is just a number wearing a costume. Next, we'll look at how banks catch fraud in milliseconds.

_windows_note: Output-timeline windows on render.py's real 24fps extract grid: each segment's rendered duration is ceil((end-start)*24)/24, not the raw source span. Verified against rendered clips where measurable. Overlay start_in_output values are derived from THESE numbers.
_overlay_gap_audit: Gaps >= 0.5s are deliberate returns to the talking head (ep13 shipped 1.0-6.7s gaps at 49-54% coverage). Anything shorter is closed to exactly zero, per rule 12 -- a sub-half-second hole reads as a bare-footage flash, not a breath. EP19 tradeoff->payoff is contiguous for exactly this reason: its beats butt up against each other and a 0.3s gap would have landed on the punchline.
_hook_lead_note: slot_hook starts at 0.000 on purpose. Its beat also starts at 0.000, so the usual >=0.25s lead would mean waiting on the title card. This slot is a transparent/right-side format specifically so it can run SIMULTANEOUSLY with the title (rule 10) -- making it opaque would delay its content until 2.766 and the beat's idea would land late, which is the EP7 hook mistake. The content is ambient (a scrolling column / a streaming URL), not a claim that needs the narration to establish it first.
_zoom_note: Gradual CENTERED zoom on the talking head. focal (540,960) = exact frame centre, not render.py's eye-line default. Direction alternates per segment so each range starts at the scale the previous one ended on -- the drift is continuous across every cut instead of snapping back to 1.0 at each edit. Magnitude capped at 4.5%: the overlays were placed against measured face positions with clearances as tight as 40px, and a centered zoom displaces a point by distance_from_centre*(Z-1), so 4.5% costs the tightest one ~13px while 12% would cost it ~35px and push graphics into the face.
